beats.text: The wind turns, and with it comes the warm, grassy musk of a horse foal that has strayed from its herd.
You drop until your belly brushes the frost-stiff stems. One paw, then the next. The foal tears at a tuft and swings its head away, and its ears flick at a fly and nothing else.
Three bounds. The grass whips your face, and the foal is only beginning to turn when your weight takes it down. Your sabers find the throat the way they were made to.
Afterwards you eat crouched low, ears turning to every sound. In the Vale, a kill out in the open draws company fast.
The wind turns, and with it comes the warm, grassy musk of a horse foal that has strayed from its herd.
You creep closer, closer, until you can hear it chewing. Then a stem snaps under your hind paw, louder than any stem has a right to be.
The foal's head snaps up. It squeals once and is gone, a brown streak racing back toward the herd, and the mares are already wheeling to meet it.
You stand in the flattened grass with your heart pounding and your belly still empty.
You know this scent before you see who it is. {catName} is waiting on a flat stone where the path bends.

npc_initiative.mistwood.request_help.v1.text: {catName} steps out of the marsh fog, muddy to the shoulders. “Our elders haven't eaten in days, and there aren't enough hunters left to feed them. Could you bring me a hare from these marshes, or anything small? I'll carry it to them myself.”

beats.text: Fog lies thick on the marsh. You're lying still in the reeds when you hear a paw pull out of the mud behind you.
{catName} steps out of the fog, muddy to the shoulders, and stops a little way off.
“Don't call out. I don't want anybody hearing us.”
“Quietly, please. Voices carry in this fog, and I don't want mine carried home.”
“Quietly, please! I know, I came to you. I just don't want the dens hearing us.”

“Our elders haven't eaten in days. We lost too many hunters when the ice broke, and there aren't enough of us left to feed everybody. Our leader would say a Mistwood cat doesn't beg from strangers. Well, I'm asking anyway.”
“Do you hunt on your own? Is it hard?”
“Could you bring me a hare from these marshes, or anything small? I'll carry it to them myself, and nobody needs to know where it came from.”

gossip.bonefieldBorder: “Bonefield's been pushing at the marsh edge. I keep finding their scent there, so I can't hunt the far reeds any more.”

replies.ask: “They'd say no, and then they'd keep an eye on me. Since the Breaking, everybody keeps an eye on everybody.”
replies.decline: “I understand. Forget you saw me out here. Please.”
replies.reminder: Did you find me a hare? Anything small from these marshes would do.
replies.kept: {catName} takes the meat gently, the way you'd carry a cub. “They'll eat tonight. Thank you.”
replies.broken: {catName} keeps a little distance. “So nothing's coming. All right. I'll manage.”
